title: Meridian: Compact Pool Lifecycle Console for Dedicated GPU Ops
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, operator-focused console surface (Meridian) that consolidates GPU pool health, autoscale controls, burst scheduling, cost delta preview, and rollout controls into a single compact panel suitable for high-density ops views and quick triage. The goal is to reduce cognitive overhead when responding to pool-level incidents and to provide safe, fast controls for canary/burst actions without navigating deep settings pages.
acceptance_criteria: Meridian panel shows key KPIs: GPU utilization avg/p95, queue length, median latency, SLO breach indicator, and burst budget remaining
Quick actions available: Toggle autoscale policy preset, schedule one-off burst, and initiate canary rollback/rollout with guarded confirmation
Cost preview displays estimated 1hr and 24hr delta for burst/autoscale changes before commit
Component fits within a single compact card (max height 320px) and has accessible keyboard focus order
Prototype usability test (n=6 operators) achieves median task completion time <= 90s for burst scheduling and <= 60s for autoscale preset switch
comments: 2026-03-09 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial kickoff. Mapped user goals from SRE interviews: fast triage, minimal clicks for burst, visible cost impact. Drafted low-fi wireframes and two interaction patterns (inline modal vs slide-over for confirmations).

2026-03-10 - Jonah Park: Pulled telemetry breakdown from infra: average pool window is 12m and burst events are 3-6min. This suggests defaults for burst duration and smoothing on the utilization sparkline. Added ENG-112041 as dependency for telemetry micro-API to support 1m granularity.

2026-03-11 - Marta Alvarez (PM): Preference for guarded defaults — autoscale toggles should surface recommended presets with a one-click preview. Request to include cost projection (1hr/24hr) and link to cost center tagging. Marked potential enterprise label requirement.

2026-03-12 - Design review: Jonah walked team through mid-fi. Feedback: make SLO breach indicator color-coded but also include an icon+tooltip for color-blind accessibility; compress action buttons into an overflow menu on narrow viewports. Action: update keyboard flows and add aria labels.

2026-03-13 - Usability session (n=6): Observed confusion around 'burst budget' wording — participants read as monetary budget. Updated copy to 'burst quota (GPU-min)'. Task times: autoscale toggle median 54s, schedule burst median 88s. Two participants requested a quick-cancel for scheduled bursts.

2026-03-14 - Engineering sync: Agreed on telemetry endpoints and a safe API contract for autoscale changes (idempotent policy patches + dry-run cost endpoint). ENG owners: Priya Reddy (ENG-112041) and Mateo Lin (ENG-112423). Noted rollout guard requirement; add audit log event for every manual burst/autoscale change.
usability_findings: Rename 'burst budget' to 'burst quota (GPU-min)' to avoid cost confusion
Add quick-cancel action for scheduled bursts to reduce operator anxiety
Provide inline cost preview to prevent accidental high-cost operations
Ensure confirmation modals show a small change diff (resources and estimated cost) and require typed confirmation for >= Configured threshold
design_decisions: Compact card layout (3-column grid): left: sparkline + SLO strip, center: KPI badges and utilization histogram, right: actions + cost preview
Default burst duration set to 10 minutes with a one-click 'extend' option, based on telemetry of typical burst events
Autoscale presets will be displayed as labeled chips with a hover preview of expected throughput and unit cost
Use slide-over for full policy editing to keep the compact card focused and fast
next_steps: Address accessibility feedback: color contrast audit and keyboard navigation tests (owner: Jonah)
Finalize Figma annotations and handoff tokens (owner: Aisha)
Create engineering tickets for dry-run cost endpoint and audit events (owners: PM + ENG)
Run an extended usability test with platform SREs (n=12) and iterate on copy and cancel flow
